idiom_name: facade with a private worker and public_send dispatch, frozen monitor object
implementation_notes: Ruby's private and protected are enforced by the interpreter - a private method cannot be called with an explicit receiver - but the same runtime documents send as calling any method of the object while public_send calls only public ones, and that pair is the whole mediation lever: the monitor is a facade whose mediated operations are public, whose workers are private, and whose dispatch of a caller-supplied name goes through public_send against an allow-list, never through send. Freeze the monitor after construction (Object#freeze refuses further modification) and mark the policy constant private_constant so constant lookup does not expose it, remembering that dup returns an unfrozen shallow copy and Marshal reconstructs objects without running the checks in initialize. None of this is tamperproof: instance_variable_get, remove_method, Module#prepend, define_method and eval all reach or replace the monitor, so the facility that resists hostile code is the process or OS boundary.
code_sketch:
class ReferenceMonitor
  POLICY = PolicyStore.new
  private_constant :POLICY                 # rules are not reachable through constant lookup
  def initialize(subject) = (@subject = subject).tap { freeze }   # no mutation after setup
  def read(id)                             # every access to the ledger passes through here
    raise SecurityError, "no principal" unless @subject.principal
    raise SecurityError, "denied: #{id}" unless POLICY.allows(@subject.principal, :read, id)
    fetch(id)                              # private worker, not callable with a receiver
  end
  private
  def fetch(id) = STORE.get(id)
end
pitfalls: send bypasses visibility entirely and public_send is the only safe dispatch: any code path that calls send with caller-influenced input defeats the facade, so the allow-list belongs next to the call.

Reflection and reopening defeat the monitor: instance_variable_get/set, Method#unbind, remove_method, Module#prepend and monkey patching can read the policy or replace the decision method, and freeze only protects that one object.
dup and clone hand out unfrozen copies and Marshal round-trips rebuild objects without running initialize, so a frozen monitor is not a frozen class and its invariants can be bypassed.

private_constant hides a constant from the public namespace but const_get still finds it, and protected is not a weaker private that is safe to ignore: it permits explicit receivers inside the same class hierarchy.
